reviews.title: Editors’ Choice
reviews.review: Turning the chaos of your calendar into a timeline with soothing colors, Tiimo does the unthinkable: It makes tackling your to-dos a calming (and even fun) activity.

reviews.title: Improving, but there are still problems
reviews.review: I fully acknowledge that this app is a work in progress, and is getting a little better with every update. But there’s still a perpetual problem where as soon as Tiimo is updated, a new feature is rolled out, bugs are fixed and glitches are patched, there is always another problem or new bugs that come up when it seems to be improving. reviews.title: Sanity saver!!!
reviews.review: I don’t have an official diagnosis yet, but I have many symptoms of ADHD and just now discovering it in my 30s. I feel like so much of my life has been explained and time management has always been a struggle for me. I work full time, mostly remote, homeschool 2 of our 4 kids so far, and run a small business. reviews.title: Do Not Like the Oct 2024 Update
reviews.review: Unless I am missing something, after the update, it does not appear that there is a timer for the individual tasks in a routine. One overall timer for the entire routine is not helpful. I want to know how much time I’m spending on each task, to ensure that I’m on track to finish my routine in the desired amount of time. reviews.title: Problems & Suggestions
reviews.review: Here’s some problems I came across. (1) I have vision problems and the times in My Day are a strain to see. I suggest enlarging the font. (2) The widget will say “Right now” for a task that isn’t happening now or soon. It’ll say that for a task an hour away. To avoid confusion, I suggest it say”Upcoming” for tasks that aren’t due yet and “Right now” when it is due. reviews.title: Highly Disappointed
reviews.review: I was quite excited to try this app to help stay on task throughout the day and battle ADHD symptoms. But after using it for about a week, I couldn’t be more disappointed. It’s a fairly well-polished app and looks beautiful, but form seemed chosen over function. For example, there is no way to snooze a task or have it roll into the following day if it goes incomplete for the day; so I had to go backwards and reschedule all of the incomplete tasks for new dates. reviews.title: So Close, Save for Bugs and Crashes
reviews.review: Tiimo is a fantastic idea of an app for those with ADHD and other neurodiverse people! But it is so incredibly buggy even with the update and it’s left me frustrated when trying to habit stack my days and structure my routines. Every time I remove a routine or calendar event, I have to restart the app to see the results or the app crashes in the process of moving events around. reviews.title: This App Changed My Life
reviews.review: I can’t express what Tiimo is to me as an app and the degree to which it has changed my life. I encourage every neurodivergent person I know to try it. I have struggled my entire life with time blindness and staying current with my self care routines. I am a person who desperately needs routines to function but has trouble maintaining them. I built my routines into the app and add them to my schedule daily and it helps me figure out more than any other tool I’ve tried how to carve out that time
